facts.text: Das Stue sits in the heart of Berlin's embassy district.
facts.excerpt: Right in the heart of Berlin’s embassy district.

facts.text: The hotel is just steps from the zoo.
facts.excerpt: Just steps from the zoo.

facts.text: The hotel is next to the Berlin Zoo and Tiergarten park.
facts.excerpt: with an enviable location next to the Berlin Zoo and Tiergarten park

facts.text: The hotel occupies a 1930s neoclassical stone building that was once home to the Royal Danish Embassy.
facts.excerpt: A grand 1930s neoclassical stone building, once home to the Royal Danish Embassy

facts.text: The high-ceilinged lobby has an original white marble staircase.
facts.excerpt: The high-ceilinged lobby, with its magnificent original white marble staircase

facts.text: Designer Patricia Urquiola furnished the lobby with modern furnishings of her own design and leather animals.
facts.excerpt: designer Patricia Urquiola has made the dramatic space cozier with comfortable modern furnishings of her own design and quirky leather animals throughout

facts.text: The public spaces display mesh sculptures of monkeys by Benedetta Mori and a crocodile head by Quentin Garel.
facts.excerpt: mesh sculptures of monkeys by Benedetta Mori, an enormous crocodile head from Quentin Garel

facts.text: Photographs by Diane Arbus and Helmut Newton hang on the walls.
facts.excerpt: photos by celebrated shutterbugs including Diane Arbus and Helmut Newton gracing the walls

facts.text: Rooms are spread through the landmark building and a newer annex.
facts.excerpt: are spread throughout the landmark building and a newer annex

facts.text: Patricia Urquiola designed the room interiors, mixing modern and classic furnishings, rich fabrics and warm woods.
facts.excerpt: Patricia Urquiola worked her magic with the interiors, resulting in a fusion of high-end modern and classic furnishings, rich fabrics, and warm woods.

facts.text: Some rooms have lofty ceilings and huge windows with views of the zoo and Tiergarten.
facts.excerpt: Some rooms feature lofty ceilings and huge windows with views of the zoo and Tiergarten

facts.text: Bathrooms have rain showers and/or freestanding bathtubs.
facts.excerpt: Bathrooms have rain showers and/or freestanding bathtubs

facts.text: All rooms have Nespresso machines and mini-bars.
facts.excerpt: All rooms have Nespresso machines and mini-bars.

facts.text: The hotel has an indoor pool and a sauna.
facts.excerpt: A nice-sized indoor pool and sauna are ideal when the Berlin weather isn't cooperating.

facts.text: The spa is the Susanne Kaufmann Spa, specializing in anti-aging treatments.
facts.excerpt: The high-end Susanne Kaufmann Spa specializes in anti-aging treatments.

facts.text: Guests get exclusive access to the neighboring zoo via the bar's terrace, skipping the entrance lines but still paying for a ticket.
facts.excerpt: you’ll still have to pay for a ticket, but you can skip the long entrance lines

facts.text: The hotel is godparent to a kangaroo named Stuy at the Berlin Zoo.
facts.excerpt: Not only our godchild the kangaroo Stuy is happy about a visit

facts.text: The hotel offers a 'Wild day in the Zoo' special for visiting the Berlin Zoo.
facts.excerpt: Wild day in the Zoo

facts.text: The Carte Blanche restaurant serves French culinary classics in a brasserie-style setting.
facts.excerpt: At Carte Blanche, experience the finest French culinary classics in a warm and inviting brasserie-style setting.

facts.text: The hotel has a bar.
facts.excerpt: Artful interior design, French cuisine, and a bar with character come together

facts.text: The hotel restaurant is Cinco by Paco Perez, serving molecular gastronomy.
facts.excerpt: Experiment with molecular gastronomy at the celebrated one-Michelin-starred Cinco by Paco Pérez

facts.text: The hotel can pick guests up from Berlin Brandenburg Airport (BER).
facts.excerpt: We are happy to pick you up from the Berlin Brandenburg Airport - BER.

facts.text: The hotel's address is Drakestrasse 1, 10787 Berlin.
facts.excerpt: Drakestrasse 1

facts.text: The hotel hosts meetings and events.
facts.excerpt: Meetings and events at Das Stue become special experiences.

facts.text: Breakfast is not included in the room rate.
facts.excerpt: breakfast isn't included in the room rate

facts.text: Das Stue calls itself a sanctuary for all the senses.
facts.excerpt: Das Stue is a sanctuary for all the senses: quiet, elegant, and unique.

contradictions.note: Official site (p1) names Carte Blanche serving French cuisine; the older Conde Nast Traveler review (p4) names Cinco by Paco Perez molecular gastronomy and a tapas-style Casual Restaurant.

sources.excerpt: At Carte Blanche, experience the finest French culinary classics in a warm and inviting brasserie-style setting.
Experiment with molecular gastronomy at the celebrated one-Michelin-starred Cinco by Paco Pérez
